title: Multimodal associations between posterior hippocampus glutamate metabolism, visual cortex connectivity, and intrusive trauma reexperiencing symptoms
title_zh: 后部海马体谷氨酸代谢、视觉皮层连通性与创伤侵入性再体验症状的多模态关联
abstract: Hippocampal dysfunction is implicated in posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), particularly intrusive reexperiencing symptoms, and may be mediated by glutamatergic excitotoxicity. Markers of glutamate dysfunction (higher glutamate to N-acetyl aspartate levels; Glu/NAA) in the hippocampus (HPC) have been linked to reexperiencing symptoms. However, the HPC demonstrates heterogeneity along its anterior-posterior axis, with different functional connectivity patterns and PTSD symptom associations, motivating investigations into glutamate metabolism in anterior and posterior HPC subregions (a/pHPC). To this end, 121 symptomatic trauma-exposed adults with current trauma reexperiencing symptoms completed magnetic resonance spectroscopy and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging to examine the regional specificity of HPC Glu/NAA associations with reexperiencing symptoms and the link to a/pHPC functional connectivity. PTSD symptoms were assessed with the Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale for DSM-5. Reexperiencing symptom severity was associated with greater Glu/NAA in the pHPC, but not aHPC. pHPC Glu/NAA was further linked to stronger functional connectivity between the pHPC and visual cortex (VC), which in turn correlated with more severe reexperiencing symptoms. This strengthened pHPC-VC connectivity explained the shared variance between pHPC Glu/NAA and reexperiencing severity, suggesting dysregulated glutamate metabolism in the pHPC may contribute to reexperiencing symptoms through functional connectivity with the VC. These findings replicate prior work linking HPC Glu/NAA to trauma reexperiencing symptoms and provide novel evidence of this association in the pHPC, but not aHPC, which is mediated by its functional connectivity with the VC. This multimodal investigation supports translational models of glutamatergic dysfunction in trauma-related disorders and highlights new targets for pharmacological and neuromodulatory interventions.
abstract_zh: 海马功能障碍与创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）相关，尤其是侵入性再体验症状，可能由谷氨酸能兴奋性毒性介导。海马（HPC）中谷氨酸与N‑乙酰天冬氨酸（NAA）比值（Glu/NAA）升高的标志已与再体验症状相关。然而，海马在前后轴上表现出异质性，具有不同的功能连通模式和PTSD症状关联，促使人们研究前后海马（a/pHPC）亚区的谷氨酸代谢。为此，121名有创伤暴露且当前出现再体验症状的受试者完成了磁共振波谱（MRS）和静息态功能磁共振成像（rs‑fMRI），以检验海马Glu/NAA与再体验症状的区域特异性及其与a/pHPC功能连通性的关联。PTSD症状使用DSM‑5版临床评估量表（CAPS‑5）评估。再体验症状严重程度与后部海马（pHPC）的Glu/NAA呈正相关，但与前部海马（aHPC）无关。pHPC的Glu/NAA进一步与pHPC与视觉皮层（VC）之间的功能连通性增强相关，而该连通性又与更严重的再体验症状相关。增强的pHPC‑VC连通性解释了pHPC Glu/NAA与再体验严重程度之间共享的方差，提示后部海马谷氨酸代谢失调可能通过与视觉皮层的功能连通性导致再体验症状。该研究复制了先前将海马Glu/NAA与创伤再体验症状关联的结果，并提供了后部海马而非前部海马与视觉皮层功能连通性介导的这一关联的新证据。此多模态研究支持创伤相关障碍中谷氨酸能功能障碍的转化模型，并突出了药物和神经调制干预的新靶点。
